title: Minimum Time to Complete All Deliveries
summary: Given two integer arrays d and r, where d = [d1, d2] represents the number of deliveries each of the two drones must complete, and r = [r1, r2] represents the recharging interval for each drone (in hours), determine the minimum total time (in hours) required to complete all deliveries.
statement: Given two integer arrays d and r, where d = [d1, d2] represents the number of deliveries each of the two drones must complete, and r = [r1, r2] represents the recharging interval for each drone (in hours), determine the minimum total time (in hours) required to complete all deliveries. Only one drone can make a delivery at any given hour, and each drone must recharge every ri hours, during which it cannot make deliveries.
constraints: d and r each contain exactly two positive values; delivery counts may reach one billion.
Drone i cannot deliver at hours divisible by r[i], and at most one drone delivers per hour.
Return the earliest hour by which both required counts can be scheduled.
reference_solution:
def minimum_delivery_time(d,r):
    from math import gcd
    common=r[0]//gcd(r[0],r[1])*r[1]
    def possible(time):
        first=time-time//r[0];second=time-time//r[1];either=time-time//common
        return first>=d[0] and second>=d[1] and either>=d[0]+d[1]
    low=1;high=2*(d[0]+d[1])+max(r)
    while not possible(high):high*=2
    while low<high:
        middle=(low+high)//2
        if possible(middle):high=middle
        else:low=middle+1
    return low

hints: For a candidate time T, count hours available to each drone and hours available to at least one drone.
Individual counts are T-floor(T/rᵢ); union capacity excludes only common recharge multiples, found with the lcm.
The three Hall-style inequalities test feasibility, and binary search finds the first feasible T.
They are necessary for each job set and their union, and with only two drones they are also sufficient for a disjoint assignment.
